subject: Marketplace listing: data residency & retention alignment across AWS/GCP/Azure
content_summary: Partner asks about how Redwood guarantees region-by-region residency and deletion semantics for customers buying via AWS/GCP/Azure marketplaces; Redwood provides matrix, suggested marketplace copy, and contract phrasing; next step: one-pager and confirm AWS Marketplace wording.
messages:
From: Alex Marshall <alex.marshall@databridge.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Kozlova <elena.kozlova@gcp-partner.com>
Date: 2027-05-05T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on residency/retention for marketplace listings

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call earlier. Two of our marketplace teams (AWS + GCP) asked for concrete language about where customer data lives when customers purchase Redwood through our listing, and what deletion / retention guarantees we can promise in the listing and in the onboarding docs. Specific asks:
- Can Redwood guarantee that data for a customer who picks an AWS region (e.g., us-east-2) will stay in that region across processing and storage?
- Do logs / audit trails or metadata ever leave that region?
- What are the default retention windows for inputs, KV cache, and backups?
- What is the deletion workflow (how fast, are there backups, is there a deletion certificate)?

We need a short, marketplace-friendly paragraph and a one-pager matrix that maps AWS/GCP/Azure options to the residency/retention behavior. Can you share those? Also attaching the partner onboarding form for completeness.

Goal: confirm wording this week so marketplaces can approve our listing.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Marshall
Marketplace Partnerships, DataBridge Cloud Partners
[Attachment: DataBridge_Partner_Onboarding_Form.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Marshall <alex.marshall@databridge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-05T18:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on residency/retention for marketplace listings

Alex — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise summary you can use verbatim for marketplace descriptions, plus a note about the longer matrix (attached). I also flagged a few items for Ben to confirm from a legal/contract perspective.

Marketplace-friendly paragraph (suggested):
"Redwood Inference supports region-specific processing and storage across AWS, GCP, and Azure. Customers selecting a public cloud region have their model inputs and generated outputs persisted in the chosen region and encrypted at rest. Metadata and control-plane routing (e.g., billing metadata, job scheduling) are retained in Redwood's control plane; for Hosted deployments the control plane may reside in a separate region depending on partner routing — for strict data residency we recommend Dedicated or Private (VPC) deployments which fully localize control-plane and storage."

Key operational points (short):
- Region pinning: Available for Hosted customers via partner routing; Dedicated and Private always respect customer-selected region for storage and inference.
- Logs & audit trails: Application logs and user-generated artifacts are retained in-region for Dedicated/Private. For Hosted, aggregated telemetry (anonymous metrics) may be processed in Redwood's control region; customer-specific audit logs are exportable on request.
- Default retention windows: Hosted (inputs/outputs): 30 days; KV cache: 7 days; backups/snapshots: 90 days. Dedicated/Private: configurable per contract (we commonly offer 30/90/365 day options).
- Deletion workflow: On request we run a secure purge job that deletes live data within 72 hours; backups are scheduled for purging according to the backup retention window (90 days default). Customers receive a deletion confirmation report; for Dedicated/Private we can support shorter windows by agreement.

I've attached a one-page residency matrix (RBW_Marketplace_Residency_Matrix.xlsx) that maps these behaviors across AWS/GCP/Azure and deployment modes.

Next steps: Ben — can you confirm the recommended default retention numbers and the standard contract clause we should push into marketplace listings? Alex/Elena — if that paragraph looks good I can produce a one-page PDF for the AWS Marketplace copy review.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: RBW_Marketplace_Residency_Matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Alex Marshall <alex.marshall@databridge.com>
Date: 2027-05-06T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on residency/retention for marketplace listings

On Thu, May 6, 2027 at 08:05 AM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai> wrote:
> I've attached a one-page residency matrix...

Quick legal/ops additions — suggested marketplace wording (short block you can paste into listing):
"Data residency: Data processed and stored for a customer is maintained in the selected public cloud region (AWS/GCP/Azure) for Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted deployments purchased via marketplace listings, Redwood routes processing and storage to the selected region where available; however, certain control-plane metadata and aggregated telemetry may be retained outside the customer region to provide global routing and platform reliability. Encryption at rest and in transit is enforced; integrations with customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK, Azure Key Vault) are available for Dedicated and Private. Contact Redwood for export compliance and contractual data localization commitments."

Retention & deletion legal points to include in onboarding / contract annex:
- Default retention (Hosted): inputs/outputs 30d; KV cache 7d; backups 90d.
- Deletion: Redwood will perform a secure purge within 72 hours of a verified deletion request. Backups will be retired according to the stated backup retention window; exceptions require a signed addendum.
- Certificate: Upon request Redwood will provide a deletion confirmation delivered through the partner portal or by email.

I attached a short draft doc with the exact contract clause and marketplace copy suggestions. If you want stricter guarantees (e.g., control-plane localization) we should indicate "Dedicated/Private required" in the Marketplace tile to avoid mismatched expectations.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: RBW_Marketplace_Wording_Draft.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)]

From: Alex Marshall <alex.marshall@databridge.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Elena Kozlova <elena.kozlova@gcp-partner.com>
Date: 2027-05-06T09:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on residency/retention for marketplace listings

Vanessa / Ben — this is exactly what we needed, thanks. Couple quick follow-ups:
1) Please produce the one-page PDF marketplace copy (we'll need separate short copy for AWS, GCP, Azure portals — but the paragraph you provided is perfect as the base).
2) Can you confirm whether the deletion confirmation is machine-generated (API/hook) or manual? For our partner listing automation we prefer an API/hook so we can show a status in our partner portal.
3) For AWS Marketplace they ask that we state whether KMS is customer-managed. Your note that KMS integration is available for Dedicated/Private — can we mark the Marketplace tile: "Customer-managed KMS available (Dedicated/Private)"?

If you can share the one-pager and the signed contract clause by EOD Friday we can push to the AWS review queue early next week. Attaching our onboarding form again.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Marshall
Marketplace Partnerships, DataBridge Cloud Partners
[Attachment: DataBridge_Partner_Onboarding_Form.pdf (application/pdf)]
